title: pr-body-claim.v1 — the judgment-bearing narrative a session supplies for coordinator-composed PR bodies
description: The compact typed input the Build coordinator's `contract` verbs render into a complete pull-request body. It carries ONLY what requires human/AI judgment or is observable solely by the session: narrative sections, falsifiable behaviors, operator-safe finding summaries, closing intent, honest caveats, and live-helper availability. Everything deterministic — the consent preamble, the change profile, spec-derived acceptance steps, validation results, reviewer-disagreement lines, reviewed/final commits and divergence, close-linkage — is supplied by the coordinator from observed facts and is NOT accepted here. All content values are single-line Markdown fragments; the renderer owns headings, bullets, emphasis, spacing, and machine markers. The fillable template emits null and empty arrays so ordinary schema validation catches an unfilled slot without grading prose.

release_impact.description: The SemVer impact this pull request declares, chosen by COMPATIBILITY (not size, effort, or importance): none = no public release impact; patch = a backward-compatible change to an existing feature; minor = a new capability or an explicit deprecation; major = an incompatible change to public behaviour, an API, or a contract. The release action folds these declarations to derive the next version (StarshipSuperjam/engine-template#942). This is the ONE judgment slot the session supplies for versioning; the renderer projects it to the visible line and the machine marker. It is independent of the pull-request title kind (Feature/Fix/…), which only groups the release notes. The fillable template emits null here, so an unfilled slot fails validation and must be chosen deliberately.

linkage.description: Explicit closing intent. `closes` and `part_of` must each be unique and must be disjoint from each other (a coordinator check, since JSON Schema cannot express cross-array disjointness). A durable Build Issue already linked by plan promotion is added by the coordinator; no originating Issue is inferred as closed.

purpose.description: Leads with the need, then the mechanism. `problem` should name the concrete prior failure or gap this closes, with any issue, decision-record, or incident cross-reference written inline — the renderer cannot invent an anchor the session does not supply.

scope.description: What this change includes, naming the real modules/verbs. The machine-generated change profile is added by the coordinator beneath these bullets; do not restate size or counts here. Behaviors render under this section but are supplied separately below.

behaviors.description: Falsifiable capabilities this change delivers, each naming the test(s) that prove it — or an explicit reason none is observable. This is the section most at risk of flattening, so the claim→test pairing is structural, not prose.

out_of_scope.description: Exclusions framed as reasoned boundaries, not a to-do list. Each item states what is excluded AND why (separate concern / deferred by operator decision / pre-existing vector), with an optional cross-reference to the tracking issue or governing eADR.

risk.description: Risks in ranked order (array order is the ranking), each with the bound that contains it. Flag the single most safety-sensitive edit. The floored-file list and guardrail tier are supplied by the coordinator; `guardrail_note` carries only the judgment of why the tier is what it is. `accepted_residual` records a residual the operator has knowingly accepted, tied to a coordinator finding id and the operator's dated decision.

demonstration.description: An operator-runnable step that drives the real changed surface and can genuinely FAIL — stated as pass-signal vs fail-signal — or a reference to the coordinator-rendered spec-derived acceptance steps, or an explicit non-observable reason. The absence of a settled specification is NOT a valid reason here (that clears only the spec-derived lane).

validation.description: The mechanical validation results, commit binding, log digests, and index-regeneration facts are supplied by the coordinator. The claim carries the section's framing (summary + Impact, so these prominent lines are authored not templated), honest caveats a green run would otherwise hide (an open fail-open finding belongs here), and the session-only observation of whether live helpers were available.

caveats.description: Honest disclosures a bare green report would drop: a named unrelated flake, a check that could not be evaluated locally, a helper that was unavailable and so left an area unverified. Empty only when the run is genuinely clean with nothing to disclose.

live_helpers.description: Session-only: whether the engine's live helpers (MCP substrate) answered this session. When any were unavailable, name each with the canonical provider diagnosis; the change was authored on the committed-file fallback.

review.description: Review depth, coverage, reviewer-disagreement lines, reviewed/final commits, and measured divergence are supplied by the coordinator. The claim carries the section's framing (summary + Impact, so these prominent lines are authored not templated), the operator-safe summary for each current coordinator finding (matched exactly to the live finding set), the free-form review→repair→re-review narrative (one entry per round or theme, so a multi-round story reads as the exemplars' bold-led bullets rather than one flat line), and the judgment of whether the merged version differs materially from the reviewed one.

finding_summaries.description: One operator-safe summary per current coordinator finding. IDs must match the live finding set exactly (a coordinator check). The private reference, if any, is optional and rendered only as a plain follow pointer; raw reviewer finding text is never published.

files_of_interest.description: The few paths that most determine this change's behavior and its acceptance referent — a curated selection (never the whole diff), each with the role it plays, ordered by importance.

ai_involvement.description: Which tool(s) and model(s) did the work, which decisions the operator made rather than the AI, and where design judgment is load-bearing versus mechanical.

operator_decisions.description: Decisions escalated to and made by the operator. Kept internally consistent with Risk's accepted_residual and the review disagreements the coordinator renders.

line.description: A single-line Markdown fragment: non-empty, no embedded newline. The renderer owns all multi-line structure, so a claim cannot inject a list break or split a section across lines; a stray line-leading marker (e.g. `## `) inside a value does not create a real section either — it fails the completeness gate (the section's Impact line is no longer detected), so preview/apply report the body incomplete rather than publishing it.
